lines.text: Finland invites every woman to free breast screening, and aims for eighty percent attendance.
The county furthest behind is not rural. It is Helsinki.
Equal Care Finland shows where cancer care falls behind, why, and what the national roadmap says to do.
The core is a simulated population.
From Statistics Finland tables, we rebuild Helsinki's women as 771 resident types: age, language, education, work.
Gemini's Decisions API judges each type once: will she attend, and what stops her?
It returns a probability and a barrier, and any dot opens the exact question behind it.
Against real attendance in 22 counties, it correlates at 0.84.
It overstates the language gap, and the app shows that.
A second engine, Jev, answers the same questions, so effects come as a range.
Invitations in a person's own language bring 992 to 2,093 more women a year, across two models.
And it cites the roadmap: action 1.3.1, page 33.
And beyond screening: the rest of the pathway.
In Satakunta, 37.5 percent of oncology patients wait over ninety days, against 3.5 nationally.
That is eight patients, so the app warns about small numbers.
Gemini writes the words. Code inserts and checks every number.
Equal Care Finland. Where the gap is, why, and what to do next.
